plugin_description: Which apps use your CPU, RAM, GPU and VRAM: a bar readout, a sortable panel with kill actions, and a desktop widget.

cpu_scale.description: Share of the whole CPU, or of one core like top and htop (a process maxing 4 cores shows 400%).
cpu_scale.label: CPU percentages
cpu_scale.machine: Share of the whole CPU (all cores = 100%)

desktop_show_graph.description: CPU and GPU usage over the last 60 samples.
desktop_show_graph.label: Show usage graph

desktop_title.description: Heading on the tile. Leave empty to hide the header row.
desktop_title.label: Title

group_by_app.description: Add up processes of the same program into one row (a browser's or game's helper processes). Off: every process gets its own row.
group_by_app.label: Group by app

interval_ms.description: How often processes are sampled. At 2000 ms the sampler uses well under 1% of one core.
interval_ms.label: Refresh interval (ms)

metric.description: Which resource decides the busiest app. Overall picks whichever resource the app strains most, as a share of the machine.
metric.label: Busiest by

rows_per_metric.description: The sampler sends the top N processes by CPU, RAM, GPU and VRAM. Raise it if the panel filter misses idle processes.
rows_per_metric.label: Rows kept per metric

show_app_icon.description: Put the busiest app's icon (or its first letter) in front of its name on the bar.
show_app_icon.label: App icons

show_temps.description: From Noctalia's system monitor, the same sensors the built-in widgets read.
show_temps.label: Show CPU and GPU temperature

ui.overall_tooltip: Sort by whichever resource each app strains most
ui.waiting_desktop: Waiting for data… Is the System Monitor Expanded plugin enabled?
